summary: receipt-is-closing-commit (S4/CRX0) and bus-RELEASE (S5) are now ENFORCED orchestrator close gates, not prose. orchestrate.ps1 Get-LegState no longer greens a leg 'done' on receipt-file existence: a worktree receipt reaches 'done' only when it is committed as the branch HEAD (W5H) AND an explicit RELEASE line for its claim is on the bus; otherwise the leg holds at a new 'closing' state with a Notify naming the exact missing condition. The existing state read was WRAPPED at :151, not rebuilt, and the gate runs before the DryRun short-circuit so a dry run exercises the identical checks. bus.py gained has_release() + a 'released' CLI - the S5 gate consumer open_claims() never had.

acceptance.predicate: done requires receipt==HEAD + RELEASE; three violation refusals with exact messages
acceptance.evidence: probe: harness/notes/receipts/w6gate_close_gate_probe.ps1, run first-hand PROBE_EXIT=0 against the REAL Get-LegState (dot-sourced lib-mode, -DryRun) over one scratch leg walked through each condition. V1 receipt-not-committed -> closing: 'receipt <r> exists in the worktree but is not committed on <branch> - writing the receipt is not finishing, committing it is (W5H)'. V2 receipt-not-HEAD -> closing: 'receipt <r> is committed (<sha8>) but is not the branch HEAD (<sha8>) - the receipt must land as the branch's closing commit (W5H)'. V3 no-bus-RELEASE -> closing: 'receipt is the closing commit but no RELEASE line for <id> is on the bus (<wave>) - post an explicit release at close (S5)'. OK clean-close -> done. Three refusals, three exact messages, then a clean pass.
